samples.summary: Vacuous test: 'plain-text serialization is unaffected' cannot fail whether the feature works or not
samples.evidence: The test asserts `serializeText({ blocks: [bulletedHeading] })` contains 'Quarterly results'. packages/docs/src/serialize/text.ts never reads `headingLevel` for any block type (blockToText switches only on horizontal-rule/page-break/table, otherwise emits inline text), so the assertion holds for any `headingLevel` value, including an implementation that treated the remembered level as a real heading. It is presented as part of the 'a remembered heading level is inert' invariant suite but proves nothing about inertness.

samples.summary: No test covers nested-table sanitization or the new MAX_TABLE_DEPTH cap
samples.evidence: `sanitizeTableData`/`sanitizeCell`/`sanitizeBlocks` recurse with a depth counter and bail at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_DEPTH`. verdict.reason: The claimed gap is real. `sanitizeTableData` recurses through `sanitizeCell(cell, depth + 1)` → `sanitizeBlocks(blocks, depth)` → `sanitizeBlock` → `sanitizeTableData(..., depth)` and returns undefined at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_DEPTH` (clipboard.ts:59, 231-243, 255-266, 313-318), with `sanitizeBlock` returning null (dropping the block) for a table whose tableData is unrecoverable. I searched by module import rather than by symbol name: only four test files import from src/view/clipboard.js — clipboard.test.ts (the sanitizer tests), image-paste-merge.test.ts (WAFFLEDOCS_MIME only, image-inline payloads), list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts (serializeClipboard; the file contains no occurrence of "table"), and table-merge-normalize.test.ts (cloneTableCells only, not the sanitizer). Every table case in the 'clipboard payload validation' describe is single-level: createTableBlock(2,3) with paragraph cells (254-272), columnWidths defaults (309-315), short-row/span clamp (317-327), and a tableCells payload whose cell holds a heading block (329-338). Nested-table coverage exists only in model/nested-table.test.ts and view/nested-table-layout.test.ts, which never call the clipboard serializers. No e2e suite exists, and only clipboard.test.ts and image-paste-merge.test.ts construct `version: 1` payloads anywhere under packages/**. So a depth-accounting mistake that silently dropped inner tables on every internal paste, or a broken MAX_TABLE_DEPTH trim, would not fail any test — a new behavior on the required paste path with no meaningful coverage, which is in-lane and blocking for the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: The text-box editor's `toggleList` exit change ships with no behavioral test
finding.evidence: The diff changes three parallel `toggleList` implementations to exit through `unlistedBlockType`: `view/editor.ts` (covered by `list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts` → 'toggleList round trip'), `view/text-editor.ts` (covered by 'keyboard bullet shortcut round trip'), and `view/text-box-editor.ts:1125` — which has no coverage. The only existing test touching it is `packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:327` ('exposes toggleList, indent, outdent'), which asserts `typeof api.toggleList === 'function'` and `expect(() => api.toggleList('unordered')).not.toThrow()` on a paragraph with no selection — it passes identically whether the exit produces a heading or a paragraph, so it is fake coverage for this change. Ironically the new test file's own comment says both toggleList paths 'must exit through unlistedBlockType or the keyboard path silently drifts', yet only two of the three named implementations are exercised.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists. packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:617-682 has a describe block 'text-box editor toggleList round trip' whose doc comment explicitly names initializeTextBox as "the third toggleList implementation" that "must exit through unlistedBlockType". Its mountTextBox helper (lines 633-647) instantiates the real editor via initializeTextBox imported from ../../src/view/text-box-editor.js (line 7) with a real canvas, no mocking of the logic under test. The first test (649-658) toggles a bulleted Heading 2 on and off and asserts getBlockType() returns {type:'heading', headingLevel:2}; the second (660-670) asserts a paragraph stays a paragraph with headingLevel undefined; the third (672-681) covers switching bullet kind and still recovering Heading 3. These assertions discriminate the change: they fail if the exit hardcoded 'paragraph' instead of unlistedBlockType. getBlockType (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1093-1102) reads real state from doc.findBlock and returns type/headingLevel, and toggleList (1121-1137) is the exact path containing the unlistedBlockType call at line 1125. The reviewer also mis-describes the test file's comment as naming only two paths; a third comment block names the text-box path. The finding's absence premise is false.
